copy_assumptions: Reception uses the same venue as the wedding because no separate reception venue was provided.
Bride honorific Srmt. is preserved exactly as requested.
The ceremony date and morning time are 7 February 2020 at 8:00 a.m.; reception is 6 February 2020 at 7:30 p.m.
Both families are represented together on the blessing plaque to retain twelve visual scenes.
image_style: A full-bleed portrait 9:16 frame of a richly cinematic dimensional storybook-animation South Indian wedding invitation. Warm honey sandstone with intricate hand-carved dark recesses, deep amber shadows, vermilion silk, ivory, aged gold, orange marigolds, white jasmine and green mango leaves. Premium animated adult characters with sculpted expressive faces, never photographic people. DRAMATIC CHIAROSCURO: strong warm back-and-side sunlight streams diagonally through open stone bays and roof gaps, clearly visible volumetric god rays cutting through thin atmospheric incense haze; luminous rim light on silk, jewelry and gold frames against darker shade. Preserve readable highlights, not a flat uniformly bright golden wash. Very fine dust motes sparkle only inside the sunbeams. Floor is subtly reflective worn stone, not a mirror. Gold lettering has illuminated beveled edges, warm restrained emissive bloom, luminous hairline flourishes and discrete pinpoint highlights; sharp readable counters. Dense fixed wedding garlands, brass lamps and flower rangoli. Roughly 12 to 20 tiny separate white, pale yellow and orange petals already scattered irregularly through the whole depth volume: a few soft near-lens edge petals, crisp midground petals, tiny distant petals. No confetti cannon, solid flower bunches in the air, symmetrical particle rows or dense shower from one point. All bouquets and garlands are fixed to their supports. Generate only from this text, no reference image. No watermark, interface, duplicate people, extra signs or unintended words.
particle_motion: PETALS AND LIGHT: continuous distributed slow-motion drift is present from the first frame, not triggered as a burst when the camera stops. Keep about 12-20 separate visible petals at irregular heights and depths. Petals flutter with independent phase, soft air resistance and a little side-to-side wobble; nearby petals drift roughly one tenth of picture height per second in the settled view, distant ones slower. Camera rotation produces the brief directional streaks; after braking the SAME scattered petals become calmly visible, with no sudden emission, rain sheet, confetti explosion or synchronized falling. Bouquets and garlands never detach. Fine dust motes drift inside diagonal volumetric sunrays. Gold edges and jewelry catch moving specular glints; text itself emits no smoke, gold liquid or floor beam.

image_scenes.name: Family invitation in the side courtyard
image_scenes.prompt: Eye-level view into a richly decorated SIDE courtyard bay beside the open Ganesha pavilion. One ivory invitation board stands on a low antique-gold plinth, centered in the lower two thirds, occupying 55 percent of frame width. Gold floral border and a tiny gold temple emblem. Readable large luminous gold display lettering, exact lines: '{{invitation_lines}}'. The first line is graceful expressive calligraphy, the lower lines elegant wedding display lettering, all fully within generous margins. A close garlanded square pillar occupies the extreme left foreground. The courtyard extends diagonally behind the board with an offset partial gopuram far to the right, not a straight tunnel centered behind the sign. Strong angled sunrise shafts enter from upper left. Brass diyas, rangoli, fixed flowers on the plinth, floating small separated petals. No Ganesha or little shrine is visible here. This view is reached by turning left out of the shrine, not flying forward through it.

image_scenes.name: Groom in the shaded stone hall
image_scenes.prompt: Inside a shaded long carved-stone hall with no outdoor tower visible. The consistent animated groom stands full-length in the LEFT third, natural adult proportions, all feet and hair inside frame with generous margins, occupying 62 percent of frame height. His ivory dhoti and diagonal gold-bordered angavastram leave the chest bare; no kurta or jacket. Floating on the RIGHT at chest height, spectacular fine champagne-gold calligraphy reads exactly '{{groom_title}}' on a small first line, '{{groom_name}}' on two graceful large lines below. The gold letters have bright rim-lit beveled edges, gentle amber halos and a few tiny star-like glints along the flourishes, not a signboard. Strong sunrays enter through high LEFT wall apertures, illuminating dusty air and the groom's rim against dark columns. Near columns frame the sides, lamps and garlands recede in layers, sparse slow-looking individual petals are distributed throughout the hall. There is no outdoor courtyard at the vanishing point.

image_scenes.name: Bride beside the sunlit transverse archway
image_scenes.prompt: A different open cross-passage at a RIGHT ANGLE to the groom's enclosed hall. The bride stands full-length in the LEFT third, hands gently clasped, dressed in the same vermilion-gold sari and jasmine bun described in the identity block. Natural adult proportions, figure about 62 percent of frame height. On the RIGHT floats a large exquisite luminous gold calligraphic title, exactly '{{bride_title}}' in small type above '{{bride_name}}' in large flowing thin strokes. Bright golden bevels and soft amber halo, sharp readable letters. Two foreground carved pillars frame the archway. Beyond is a SIDE VIEW across broad courtyard steps and a LOW roofed temple wing, with only an offset small portion of the tall tower near the far LEFT edge. Do not put a giant frontal gopuram centrally behind the bride. Blazing oblique sunbeams come through the far side opening, creating dramatic light shafts and glowing sari and jewelry edges against shaded stone. Garlands above, fixed lamp rows, small independent petals at varied heights. The family plaque is outside this view around the right corner.

image_scenes.name: Both families' blessing plaque in the west colonnade
image_scenes.prompt: LOW three-quarter view of an ivory family blessing plaque beside a massive carved pillar, a completely new viewing direction along the temple's WEST colonnade. Camera sees the plaque plane turned 15 degrees, its thick antique-gold frame edge catching a bright sun streak. Plaque occupies about 65 percent of image width and 64 percent of height with all corners visible. Exact gold-brown readable serif lines with glowing gold headings: '{{family_lines}}'. Both parents' groups get clear spacing. Thin embossed floral gold border and a small sacred lamp emblem above. A compact white-orange bouquet is already grounded against the plinth at its base, below all text; it is attached and stationary. The background looks SIDEWAYS across rows of columns, receding horizontally toward screen left, not through a centered aisle. No gopuram in the center, no person here. Deep shaded carved ceiling above, dramatic sunrise shafts entering from left across warm dust motes and the plaque frame. Sparse individual drifting petals are separated from the grounded bouquet.

image_scenes.name: Wedding ceremony in the inner mandap
image_scenes.prompt: Seated-eye-level THREE-QUARTER view of the wedding ritual mandap, reached by turning LEFT at a right-angle corner of the colonnade. The consistent groom and bride sit on the LEFT half on a dark red patterned ceremonial rug, groom left and bride next to him. Both now wear red-white-green flower garlands over unchanged clothes. Groom gently raises his right hand over the bride's hair, bride lowers her eyes and smiles. A small contained copper ritual fire and brass offerings are low at left, not dominating the foreground. On the RIGHT is ONE independent dark mahogany timing sign in an ornate antique-gold frame, generously sized and easy to read, exact illuminated gold lettering: '{{ceremony_lines}}'. The background is an intimate dark stone sanctum-side mandap with deep shadow, NOT a distant straight corridor. Thick garlands hang overhead and diagonal SUNRAYS from a side opening rake across the couple, haze and carved columns; warm firelight gives subtle secondary highlights. A priest is a small secondary figure far left. Quietly suspended individual petals are distributed at several depths, never a mass burst. All flower arrangements are grounded.

image_scenes.name: Venue at the north courtyard corner
image_scenes.prompt: Eye-level courtyard CORNER view facing an ornate dark-mahogany venue board on a low square gold-trimmed stone pedestal. Board is centered, about 56 percent of image width and 56 percent of height. Exact large gold serif copy with gently luminous bevel highlights: '{{venue_lines}}'. All text readable with generous margins. A CLOSE square carved column frames the extreme RIGHT foreground, side face strongly visible. The architecture behind forms an L-shaped courtyard: a low decorated temple wing stretches across the background and the tall gopuram appears only off-axis in the distant LEFT quarter. This is a sideways courtyard view, never a straight forward aisle ending at a central tower. Rich flower swags, fixed lamps, a flower rangoli beneath the board. Low sunlight cuts diagonally across haze from left, with dark sculpted shade on the near pillar and radiant gold sign edges. Small slow-looking petals distributed at different heights. No foreground couple.

image_scenes.name: Reception at the evening garden pavilion
image_scenes.prompt: An intimate evening reception pavilion beside the temple garden, BLUE HOUR sky only in a small upper background band. Warm brass-lamp pools illuminate gold drapes and dense orange-white-red flower garlands; narrow cinematic shafts from warm lights pass through faint haze, preserving deep blue shadows. An ivory reception board on a delicate antique-gold three-legged easel occupies the central 60 percent of width, all frame and legs visible. Large sharp dark-gold lettering, luminous gold title and frame edges, exact text: '{{reception_lines}}'. A carved near pillar frames camera LEFT and the garden extends sideways toward camera RIGHT, not a long centered runway. Brass lamps at varied depths, softly blurred secondary guests at the far side, fixed low flower borders. Quiet suspended white-orange individual petals and tiny warm dust motes spread irregularly through the depth. Exactly one reception board and no other signs.

image_scenes.name: Hosts in the lamp-lit side shrine hall
image_scenes.prompt: A richly decorated INNER lamp hall viewed frontally at eye height after a 90 degree left turn from the garden. ONE tall ivory host plaque supported on a low ornate gold pedestal at the top of three shallow steps. The frame is carved antique gold with tiny pink flowers at the corners. Exact large readable gold-brown lettering: '{{host_lines}}'. Plaque fills 60 percent of frame width and 57 percent of height. Symmetrical close carved pillars, numerous small hanging brass oil lamps and flower swags, dark recesses and strong warm angled shafts from high side openings. The words glow delicately at their gold edges while their faces remain crisp. The space behind the plaque is SHALLOW and shaded, no long visible tunnel behind it. The open corridor extends from the plaque back toward the camera for the backward departure. Petals are sparse, individual and evenly scattered through depth; lamps flicker warmly, rangoli and bouquets stay on the floor. No people visible.

image_scenes.name: Single couple and single date board
image_scenes.prompt: The same animated bride and groom stand close together beneath a wide stone gateway in a sunrise courtyard, bride LEFT of groom. Both retain their exact sari, dhoti, diagonal angavastram, hair, jewelry and red-white-green wedding garlands. Groom clean-shaven. Full bodies and bare feet visible, couple occupies about 57 percent of image height and the middle-left 48 percent of width. They face mostly toward the camera with small smiles, their hands gently joined at waist height, calm and affectionate. A low flower arch and the distant gopuram sit behind them on the courtyard axis. EXACTLY ONE SAVE THE DATE BOARD: a simple dark-mahogany rectangular plaque with a thin ornate gold frame on ONE fixed gold easel, standing on the far RIGHT with clear space between it and the groom. Entire board visible, about 24 percent of frame width, tilted no more than 5 degrees, with no overlapping frame, extra panel, backing sign, mirrored copy or second easel anywhere. Its exact stable gold lettering is '{{save_date_lines}}'. No other written text in the whole image. Board design is deliberately simple so it can stay rigid during animation. One hanging brass lamp is already attached to the gateway at the upper center and partly visible along the top edge. Strong diagonal sunrise god rays through the gateway, glowing rim light on the couple, deep carved shadows, subtle floor reflections. Around 12 tiny separate petals suspended at irregular heights and depths. All bouquets, garlands, columns, lamps and the single board are fixed scenery.

turns.extra: The seated ceremony and its board sweep screen left. Pivot RIGHT 90 degrees about the corner column; the venue board is in the perpendicular courtyard, not further ahead. The tower stays off-axis to the left in the new view. No forward flight through the ceremony or a doorway tunnel.

A near pillar and gold drape briefly fill the view and conceal the change to evening. No long forward approach to a distant easel. The reception easel is already near when uncovered.

turns.settle: a gentle lateral drift over 20 centimetres at constant distance from the plaque
